digest:
The day’s highlights showcase a vibrant cross‑pollination between holographic entanglement, conformal bootstrap, and higher‑point dynamics.  A striking set of counterexamples to the long‑standing conjecture that holographic entropy inequalities are free of area‑law UV divergences demonstrates that the Ryu–Takayanagi cone is far richer than previously thought, and the authors even supply a systematic recipe for generating thousands of new examples.  In parallel, a novel infrared‑safe S‑matrix for \(\mathcal N=4\) SYM—obtained by placing the theory on rigid \(\mathrm{AdS}_4\) with Dirichlet boundary conditions—turns scattering amplitudes into finite boundary correlators and yields a compact Mellin‑space expression for a one‑loop four‑point function.  Other holographic advances include a back‑reacted geometry that reproduces strange‑metal linear‑\(T\) resistivity and quadratic Hall angle, a fluid/gravity correspondence for 3d flat space with non‑compact boundaries, and a new class of hidden wormhole solutions that evade the usual mass‑inflation instability.  
On the CFT side, the community has pushed the frontier of higher‑point and higher‑genus data: explicit 2D unitary bosonic CFTs with Virasoro primary gaps of three and four at large central charge have been constructed via asymmetric orbifolds, offering fresh laboratories for holographic duals; a numerical scheme for all‑genus \(\mathcal N=1\) superconformal blocks on arbitrary Riemann surfaces has been presented, enabling efficient evaluation of higher‑point correlators in supersymmetric theories; and the structure constants of planar \(\mathcal N=4\) SYM have been reformulated in a separation‑of‑variables framework that delivers finite‑coupling three‑point functions for both BPS and Konishi operators.  Complementing these analytic advances, systematic scans of class\,S theories up to rank\,7 reveal thousands of isomorphic pairs, while 5d \(\mathbb Z_n\) S‑folds are shown to arise from cyclic isogenies of the familiar \(E_{6,7,8}\) Seiberg–Witten curves, tying together number‑theoretic structures with gauge‑theoretic dualities.  Together, these results underscore a growing synergy between holography, conformal bootstrap, and arithmetic aspects of quantum field theory.

papers.title: Isomorphisms of Class S Theories with IndexLab
papers.abstract: We use IndexLab to scan untwisted and twisted class $\mathcal{S}$ constructions based on ADE Lie algebras of rank up to seven, as well as $A_8$ and $E_8$. We consider surfaces of genus at most three with up to five punctures, covering 167,244,647 constructions in total. To find candidate pairs of isomorphic theories, we compare Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor data. We set aside pairs explained by known mechanisms, leaving a catalogue of 5,278 candidate pairs. Recurring changes in rank, puncture labels, and twists suggest families of candidate isomorphisms. We group 99.58% of the pairs into 25 families and 6 finite families. IndexLab is available at superconformal.com.
papers.summary: The authors systematically scan untwisted and twisted class S constructions up to rank 7 (plus A8, E8) on low‑genus surfaces with punctures, using the IndexLab tool to compute Schur, Hall‑Littlewood indices, anomalies, Coulomb spectra, and flavor data. They identify 5,278 candidate isomorphic pairs, organize them into 25 families plus 6 finite families, and provide the dataset for further study.

papers.title: An infrared-safe $S$-matrix for $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills
papers.abstract: Scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories are not observables: they are infrared divergent, and the standard regulators are tied either to perturbation theory or the planar limit. We study $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on rigid AdS$_4$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the role of the amplitude is played by correlation functions of boundary operators. These are finite, and they are defined at any coupling and for any gauge group. Among them, the four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is the counterpart of the $2\to2$ amplitude of the elementary supergluon states, and arguably the simplest non-trivial observable of the theory. In this paper, we compute it at weak coupling to one loop. The tree-level correlator follows directly from the microscopic theory, and the one-loop correlator, which we obtain from AdS unitarity, takes a remarkably simple form in Mellin space. In the flat-space limit, it reproduces the one-loop scattering amplitude, with the infrared divergences re-emerging as logarithms.
papers.summary: The authors formulate an infrared‑safe S‑matrix for N=4 SYM by placing the theory on rigid AdS4 with Dirichlet boundary conditions, turning scattering amplitudes into finite boundary correlators. They compute the four‑point function of the flavor‑current supermultiplet at one loop via AdS unitarity, finding a simple Mellin‑space expression that reproduces the flat‑space one‑loop amplitude when the AdS radius is taken large.

papers.title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
papers.authors: Nicholas M. K. Ross, Toby Wiseman
papers.abstract: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.
papers.summary: The paper develops a non‑perturbative Picard‑Lefschetz framework for Euclidean quantum gravity by introducing a forward‑backward gradient flow that deforms real saddle‑point metrics into complex integration cycles, reproducing the Gibbons–Hawking–Perry prescription near real saddles and extending it to non‑perturbative regimes. Numerical examples for Euclidean de Sitter and Schwarzschild geometries illustrate how the flow constructs Lefschetz thimbles and clarifies the conformal factor problem in semiclassical gravity.

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.
papers.summary: The paper establishes that non-supersymmetric AdS vacua in IIA and IIB string theory satisfy the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem when a weak fake superpotential exists, providing evidence for their absolute stability. It further shows that certain KKLT vacua lack this superpotential, leading to violations of the inequality and indicating false vacuum decay.

papers.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
papers.authors: Bercel Boldis, Nikolay Gromov, Gregory P. Korchemsky, Alessandro Testa
papers.abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.
papers.summary: This work derives exact localization identities for spectral determinants governing meson spectra in planar two‑dimensional QCD and the Ising field theory, expressing logarithmic derivatives in terms of Baxter Q‑functions at special points. By establishing a rational closure condition on the operator symbols, the authors extend these identities to a broader class of spectral problems, including generalized QCD models with quartic potentials and interpolating symbols between QCD and Ising.

papers.title: All-Genus 2D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Superconformal Blocks
papers.authors: Sam Christian, Yuchen Wang, Xi Yin, Yutai Zhang
papers.abstract: We develop a numerical algorithm for two dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks at arbitrary genera, in arbitrary plumbing channels, and for arbitrary spin structures. The algorithm utilizes two commuting copies of Virasoro subalgebras of the direct sum of the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal algebra with an auxiliary free fermion algebra, which allows us to reduce the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks to Virasoro conformal blocks.
papers.summary: The authors present a numerical method for computing 2D N=1 superconformal blocks on surfaces of any genus, using a decomposition into commuting Virasoro subalgebras of the N=1 superconformal algebra plus a free fermion. This approach enables efficient evaluation of blocks in arbitrary plumbing channels and spin structures, extending the toolkit for higher‑genus and higher‑point correlators in supersymmetric CFTs.

papers.title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
papers.abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that many holographic entropy inequalities, previously thought to be free of area‑law UV divergences, actually exhibit such divergences, providing explicit counterexamples and a systematic way to generate thousands more. This challenges earlier conjectures about the universality of the Ryu‑Takayanagi entropy cone and impacts the consistency of holographic entanglement entropy calculations.

papers.title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
papers.abstract: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;\alpha)$ factor.
papers.summary: The paper constructs new supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven‑dimensional supergravity by deforming the half‑BPS AdS$_3	imes S^3_+	imes S^3_-	imesmathbb R^2$ background, analyzing the resulting four‑form fluxes, equations of motion, and Killing superalgebras. It finds that lightlike warpings preserve four supercharges while spacelike and timelike warpings preserve eight, with a single $mathfrak d(2,1;alpha)$ factor in the symmetry algebra.

papers.title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.authors: Vahid Reza Shajiee, Mohammad Mehdi Sheikh-Jabbari, Vahid Taghiloo
papers.abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2\pi$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).
papers.summary: The authors extend covariant phase space methods to derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on arbitrary null boundaries in dynamical Einstein spacetimes, showing that entropy variation is a surface charge and temperature is the non‑affinity parameter. Their results hold even when horizon area decreases, providing a non‑stationary, non‑teleological thermodynamic framework that reproduces known dynamical entropy formulas in near‑stationary limits.

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
papers.abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlev\'e V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.
papers.summary: The paper derives the exact vacuum modular Hamiltonian for a free massive scalar field confined to an interval of length L, expressing its eigenfunctions as superpositions of plane waves emitted from the interval endpoints and solving a linear integral equation whose Neumann series captures multiple reflections. It then studies the modular flow of localized wave packets within the causal diamond, revealing non‑geometric behavior where commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the expected conformal trajectories.

papers.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
papers.abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $\theta=\pi$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.
papers.summary: This paper shows that on $mathbb{RP}^3$ torsion removes the need for twisted boundary conditions to expose mixed center anomalies in $SU(2)$ gauge theories, leading to universal level degeneracies at $	heta=pi$. By mapping the orbifold to $mathbb{R}	imesmathbb{RP}^3$ and resolving it to Eguchi–Hanson space, the authors compute the BPST instanton contribution to the gaugino condensate and demonstrate its weak‑coupling value.

papers.title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
papers.authors: Alan Garbarz, Gabriel Palau, Guillem P\'erez-Nadal
papers.abstract: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm i\beta/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.
papers.summary: The paper derives explicit formulas for the modular conjugation operator (J) for thermal states in two‑dimensional CFTs, showing that modular images correspond to real‑space fields and that complex coordinates appear only when extending to the commutant. It also presents a purification of the chiral (U(1)) current via a doubled Fock space, matching Sorce’s canonical purification and extending to all primary thermal states.

papers.title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
papers.authors: Yuri Chervonyi, Fabian Ruehle, Nenad Tomasev
papers.abstract: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level mechanisms by which complex structure moduli can generate fermion mass hierarchies and show analytically and numerically that both mechanisms are obstructed for previously studied tetra-quadric models. Motivated by these obstructions, we scan the existing databases of tens of thousands of complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models and find a unique smooth quotient admitting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix at tree level. Evaluating the physical couplings on this manifold and evolving them under the renormalization group, we obtain realistic mass hierarchies for the top, charm, up, and bottom quarks in the smooth supergravity regime.
papers.summary: The authors investigate whether tree‑level Yukawa couplings in smooth heterotic Calabi‑Yau compactifications can generate the observed quark mass hierarchies, identifying two complex‑structure–dependent mechanisms that fail for tetra‑quadric models. After scanning large line bundle databases, they find a unique quotient Calabi‑Yau where a rank‑three up‑quark Yukawa matrix yields realistic top, charm, up, and bottom masses within the supergravity regime.

papers.title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
papers.authors: Blake J. Bottesi, James T. Liu
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the partition function of a free bosonic (U(N)) multi‑matrix model can be expanded in terms of giant graviton contributions, each associated with a distinct matrix and described by a (d)-node quiver of bifundamentals. This suggests a novel holographic interpretation for non‑gravitational models, though the resulting graviton partition functions retain explicit (N)-dependence.

papers.title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
papers.authors: Alexey Litvinov, Egor Shestopalov, Nikita Slavnov
papers.abstract: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.
papers.summary: The paper develops a Fredholm-Baxter framework for the 't Hooft equation in two‑dimensional QCD, deriving exact spectral‑determinant identities (FLZ) and proving meson‑spectral nondegeneracy for arbitrary quark masses. It introduces a new class of integrable integral operators and connects their analytic structure to completely integrable Fredholm theory.

papers.title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
papers.abstract: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for $n=2$, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For $n\geq 3$, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.
papers.summary: The authors show that in 2+1 dimensional scalar field theories a negative mixed quartic coupling can trigger spontaneous symmetry breaking that persists to arbitrarily high temperatures, even generating fermion masses via Yukawa couplings. They further demonstrate that for O(2) symmetry a BKT superfluid phase survives at all temperatures, while for O(n≥3) the size of ordered domains grows with temperature, using high‑temperature expansions and functional RG.

papers.title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
papers.authors: Simon Ekhammar, Alessandro Georgoudis, Nikolay Gromov
papers.abstract: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.
papers.summary: The paper reformulates the conjecture for planar ½ N=4 SYM structure constants in a separation‑of‑variables framework, enabling non‑perturbative evaluation via the quantum spectral curve. It delivers finite‑coupling three‑point functions for two half‑BPS operators and the spin‑two Konishi state, reproducing known weak/strong limits and yielding new high‑loop and strong‑coupling data.

papers.title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
papers.authors: Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Rodrigo Olea, David Rivera-Betancour
papers.abstract: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions. At fixed total string tension, the difference of the renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time determines the relative tension work, giving a geometric interpretation of the relative thermodynamic length.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the discrepancy between holographic and topological renormalization of the Euclidean action for the AdS C-metric, separating regular curvature from conical singularities. It identifies the residual difference with Gauss–Bonnet entropy at the horizon’s conical points, offering a geometric interpretation of tension work in black hole thermodynamics.

papers.title: Non-integrability of open strings via Pohlmeyer reduction
papers.authors: Divania Carelse, Laila Tribelhorn, Konstantinos Zoubos
papers.abstract: We study integrable and non-integrable boundary conditions for classical strings from the point of view of Pohlmeyer reduction. We first consider the integrable case of strings ending on Y=0 non-maximal giant gravitons. Pohlmeyer reduction of such strings leads to a sine-Gordon model, for which a criterion for boundary integrability was provided by Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov. We confirm that the Pohlmeyer field satisfies this condition. We then turn to the main focus of our work, which is open strings on AdS3. By evaluating the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov criterion for the corresponding Pohlmeyer-reduced models, we are able to distinguish between integrable and non-integrable cases, in line with expectations from recent analytic and numerical studies. We conclude that Pohlmeyer reduction can provide a useful perspective on open-string non-integrability.
papers.summary: This paper investigates integrability of open strings in AdS3 via Pohlmeyer reduction, applying the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov boundary criterion to distinguish integrable from non‑integrable boundary conditions. The authors confirm that strings ending on Y=0 giant gravitons reduce to an integrable sine‑Gordon model, while generic AdS3 open strings exhibit non‑integrability, offering a new diagnostic tool for open‑string dynamics in holographic settings.

papers.title: Higher Spin Lagrangians for Black Holes in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects studying higher-spin Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions $D=d+1$. We first consider fields described by totally symmetric tensors with $s$ indices. At finite spin, the minimal coupling depends on both the spin and spacetime dimension. We show that, in the high-spin limit $s\gg 1$, the minimal multipolar expansion becomes dimension independent and it corresponds to the one which reproduces the Kerr solution in four dimensions. Furthermore, we identify a dimension independent relation among the non-minimal coupling coefficients that allows us to reproduce the Myers-Perry multipolar structure in arbitrary dimensions. We then extend our analysis to Lagrangians involving fields with different Young representations, which are allowed in higher dimensions.
papers.summary: The authors construct higher‑spin field Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions and analyze their minimal multipolar expansions. They show that in the large‑spin limit the expansions become dimension‑independent and reproduce the Kerr and Myers‑Perry multipolar structures, extending the analysis to mixed‑symmetry tensors.

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.
papers.summary: This paper develops a Lie-Poisson framework for dissipative spin hydrodynamics, showing that the Poincaré algebra and spin commutation relations uniquely determine reversible couplings between fluid flow and spin. It finds that spin magnitude is conserved under flow, direction undergoes Fermi-Walker transport, and dissipation induces a critical shear rate that reorients spin away from vorticity.

papers.title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
papers.authors: Bruce A. Bassett, Sergio L. Cacciatori, Ugo Moschella
papers.abstract: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincar\'e chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.
papers.summary: The authors present a coordinate‑independent method for evaluating de Sitter boundary correlators by exploiting maximal analyticity and differential–difference equations of Schwinger–Keldysh diagrams. By analytically continuing vertex integrals onto imaginary Lobachevskij cycles and applying a Mehler–Fock transform, they convert the problem into algebraic spectral recurrences, solve them with generalized hypergeometric functions, and assemble a complete spectral representation for one‑ and two‑loop boundary in‑in diagrams.

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.authors: H. Adami, R. Esp\'indola, K. Lara, A. Latifi
papers.abstract: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schr\"odinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless P\"oschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.
papers.summary: This paper extends the fluid/gravity correspondence to 3d flat gravity with non‑compact spatial boundaries, showing that the boundary charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras that map to a 2d conformal fluid stress tensor. It further explores integrable boundary conditions, a T\bar T‑type flow for the quasi‑local stress tensor, and outlines a Weyl C*‑algebra quantization, offering new insights for flat‑space holography.

papers.title: Toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds: constructions, fixed loci and O-plane charges
papers.abstract: We review the systematic construction of toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds through divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections. We relate the homogeneous-coordinate and lattice descriptions and explain the computation of fixed loci and the geometric data entering Hodge splittings and tadpole conditions. Our triangulation-wise analysis identifies multiple compatible involutions on a single triangulation and tracks their realisations across different triangulations, revealing the orientifold structure within and across toric phases. We complement this review with new calculations and explicit examples that refine the fixed-locus geometry and the associated orientifold charge data. The examples also identify coordinate representatives of the identity and invariant hypersurface families with unavoidable singularities. These results support an ongoing update of the orientifold catalogue and provide geometric input for D-brane configurations, flux compactifications and moduli stabilisation.
papers.summary: This review surveys the construction of toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds via divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections, detailing how fixed loci, Hodge splittings, and O-plane charges are computed across different triangulations. It also supplies new explicit examples and refined data useful for D-brane model building, flux compactifications, and moduli stabilization.

papers.title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
papers.authors: Nirmalendu Acharyya, Arkajyoti Bandyopadhyay, Parthsarathi Kondapure, Sachindeo Vaidya
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-G\"ursey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $g<g_\ast^{BJ}$, but become almost entirely expelled from this region for $g>g_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.
papers.summary: This study numerically explores weak‑coupling quantum phase transitions in a two‑color, one‑flavor SU(2) matrix QCD model, revealing sector‑dependent critical couplings and distinct superselection sectors on either side of the transition. The work shows that quark‑glue interactions drive localization‑delocalization behavior, with ground states becoming confined to codimension‑two submanifolds as the coupling crosses the critical value.

papers.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ S-folds, quotient curves, and isogenies
papers.authors: Sung-Soo Kim, Song Liu, Mudassar Sabir, Futoshi Yagi
papers.abstract: We construct Seiberg--Witten curves for the $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, and $\mathbb{Z}_6$ S-folds of 5d rank-1 superconformal theories. Compared with the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case arXiv:2611.09804, $\mathbb{Z}_{3,4,6}$ S-folds require stronger constraints on the mass parameters. We provide a systematic procedure of realizing the S-foldings at the mirror curve level. We obtain the same elliptic curve families by specializing the complexified mass parameters of the rank-1 $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$ theories, with holonomies motivated by the 7-brane insertions required by the S-fold prescription. The two constructions agree in Weierstrass form. The families with continuous mass deformations organize into characters of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{g}_2$, consistently with their singular fibers. Finally, we discuss that the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ S-folds can be obtained through cyclic $n$-isogenies, which may provide a uniform quotient curve description of rank-1 S-folds.
papers.summary: The authors construct Seiberg–Witten curves for 5d rank‑1 SCFTs with <z3>, <z4>, and <z6> S‑fold symmetries, showing that the curves arise from cyclic n‑isogenies of the familiar E6, E7, and E8 families and that mass deformations organize into <su(2)> and <g2> characters. They provide a systematic mirror‑curve procedure and demonstrate consistency with Weierstrass forms, offering a uniform quotient‑curve description for these rank‑1 S‑folds.

papers.title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State
papers.authors: Yongjun Ahn, Matteo Baggioli, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim
papers.abstract: Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $\rho_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cot\Theta_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry. The window is bounded by relevant deformations of the corresponding fixed point: momentum relaxation sets the upper edge, while the magnetic field $B$ closes it from below at $T_{\min}\sim B^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic corrections. At $T_{\min}$, strange-metal transport, the scaling geometry, and critical thermodynamics break down together. Our results point to intermediate criticality as a distinct route to strange-metal transport, and suggest that it can be identified by the simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamic scaling under a magnetic field.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that linear‑T resistivity and quadratic Hall angle can arise from an intermediate critical regime in holographic models, with a finite temperature window bounded by momentum relaxation and a magnetic field. The authors construct a fully backreacted geometry that reproduces both scalings and shows simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamics at a field‑dependent minimum temperature.

papers.title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
papers.authors: Julien Barrat, Alessio Miscioscia, Fedor K. Popov
papers.abstract: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll \Delta_\chi \ll \Delta^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory. For the three-dimensional Ising model, Monte Carlo simulations yield a perimeter coefficient in good agreement with a Pad\'e interpolation of our $\varepsilon$-expansion result.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a high‑temperature effective field theory for spatial conformal line defects, deriving local geometric terms that encode tension and bending. Using a convergent bulk OPE, it obtains universal asymptotic relations for defect–bulk couplings and computes explicit coefficients for several models, including the O(N) Wilson–Fisher fixed point and the 3d Ising model.

papers.title: The Pfaffian sector of $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ BPS cohomology: brane excitations, triality and fortuity
papers.abstract: We study the classical $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS cohomology of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ in the BMN sector, including the operators built with one $\epsilon$-tensor. These operators are odd under the reflection in $\mathrm{O}(2N)$, carry the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ charge of a D3-brane wrapped on $\mathbb{RP}^3\subset\mathbb{RP}^5$, and form the Pfaffian sector. For $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ we determine this sector through level $j=18$, where the level is twice the total charge of an operator. All but one of its $106$ $\mathrm{SU}(3)_R$ multiplets are products of trace gravitons and excited Pfaffians. The exception is a singlet, represented by the singlet projection of the rank-four member of a four-term family of $\epsilon$-tensor operators. We construct a covering space for the Pfaffian sector in which this family is closed at every rank, and the family defines a non-graviton class for every $N\ge 4$. Triality pairs the singlet with a reflection-even class that is fortuitous with respect to the trace covering. The two classes restrict, along the spinor and the vector embedding of $\mathfrak{so}(7)$ respectively, to the known non-graviton singlet of $\mathrm{SO}(7)$, which is lifted at first order. We show that the two $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ classes, and the family for every $N\ge 4$, are protected to all orders of perturbation theory. Their protection is compatible with the lifting in $\mathrm{SO}(7)$ because restriction to a subalgebra does not commute with the quantum corrections to the supercharge.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the Pfaffian sector of 1/16‑BPS operators in SO(2N) N=4 SYM, identifying a protected singlet and a family of ε‑tensor operators that survive quantum corrections. The authors construct a covering space and show how triality pairs the singlet with a fortuitous class, providing new insights into non‑graviton states in the BMN sector.

papers.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
papers.abstract: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at https://github.com/xingyang-yu/StringQFT.
papers.summary: StringQFT is a comprehensive 18-volume textbook collection that assembles string-theoretic constructions of quantum field theory, including brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory, wrapped M5-branes, and exact worldsheet models. It also provides AI-friendly infrastructure—open-book benchmarks, retrieval-augmented generation, local lexical retriever, and 19 calculation tools—to facilitate automated exploration and verification of theoretical physics problems.

papers.title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
papers.abstract: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors. From lattices constructed using ternary quadratic-residue codes, we obtain an infinite family with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(p+1,p+1)$ for primes $p\ge71$ with $p\equiv23\pmod{24}$. From Barnes-Wall lattices, we obtain an infinite family with gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(2^m,2^m)$ for odd $m\ge7$. We also obtain two additional examples, with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(48,48)$ and gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(512,512)$.
papers.summary: The authors construct explicit 2D unitary bosonic CFTs with a unique vacuum and a Virasoro primary gap exceeding two, using asymmetric orbifolds of even unimodular lattices and proving anomaly‑free gauging. Their infinite families with gaps three and four at large central charges provide new examples that could inform holographic duals and the structure of higher‑point conformal blocks.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.authors: Luigi Cappiello, Anton Rebhan, Shigeki Sugimoto
papers.abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.
papers.summary: This review surveys holographic QCD, contrasting top‑down constructions from probe flavor branes in the Witten model with bottom‑up AdS5 setups that incorporate global symmetries and anomalies. It discusses how these frameworks reproduce meson, baryon, and glueball spectra and outlines their phenomenological successes and limitations.

papers.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
papers.authors: J\'ulia Tartera Barber\`a, Sarah Louisa Pitz, J\"urgen Schaffner-Bielich, Laura Tolos
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $\phi^n$ self-interaction potential. By solving the coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations for boson masses between 200 MeV and 1 GeV and self-interaction strengths with $n=4$ and $n=40$, we show that strong self-interactions and higher boson masses enhance the stability of compact star configurations at high central pressures, though they reduce maximum overall masses. Ultra-compact solutions with $C \ge 1/3$ capable of mimicking black holes are significantly restricted compared to hadronic models, emerging only for strong self-interactions and dark matter fractions exceeding 90\%. Depending on the parameters, the compact stars form either extended dark matter halos or compact cores: stronger self-interactions and higher boson masses suppress the radial extension to favor compact cores of dark matter. Matching our models against observational constraints highlights PSR J1614$-$2230 and XTE J1814$-$338 as potential window of opportunity for dark matter detection. Notably, XTE J1814$-$338 could confirm a dark sector, given its requirement for light boson masses ($m_b \approx 200\text{--}300\text{ MeV}$) and strongly DM-dominated configurations.
papers.summary: The study explores how self-interacting bosonic dark matter embedded in quark stars modifies their mass-radius relations and stability, showing that strong self-interactions and heavier bosons favor compact cores but limit maximum masses. The authors identify PSR J1614-2230 and XTE J1814-338 as observational targets that could reveal dark-sector effects, especially for light bosons (~200–300 MeV).

papers.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
papers.abstract: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular, their high-frequency correlations. In this way, we show that it is possible to recover network connectivity from neural activity.
papers.summary: The paper derives analytic relations between synaptic connectivity and spike correlations in stationary recurrent neural networks, decomposing contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher-order paths. It demonstrates that experimentally measurable high-frequency correlations can be inverted to reconstruct effective connectivity.

papers.title: Renormalization-Group Foundation of Critical Modes in Correlation Matrices
papers.authors: Yanhua Zhang, Mingmei Xu, Jinghua Fu, Yuanfang Wu
papers.abstract: Based on the relevant scaling operators of renormalization-group theory, we establish a theoretical framework for constructing complete families of critical-sensitive fluctuation observables and their connected correlation matrices. The corresponding eigenstates of the correlation matrices reveal a hierarchy of multiscale critical correlation patterns and the leading normalized eigenvalues and their ratios show the finite-size scaling behavior. Applying this framework to the two-dimensional Ising model, the correlation matrices associated with both spin and energy operators are constructed. The resulting energy-sector eigenstate patterns, together with the scaling behavior of the leading eigenvalues, provide further support for the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss its potential extension to systems with unknown Hamiltonians.
papers.summary: The paper develops a renormalization‑group based framework for constructing critical‑sensitive fluctuation observables and their correlation matrices, revealing a multiscale hierarchy of eigenstates and finite‑size scaling of leading eigenvalues. Applied to the 2D Ising model, the method reproduces known energy‑sector patterns and supports the generality of the approach.

papers.title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$
papers.authors: Francesco Del Porro, Alessia Platania, Samuele Silveravalle
papers.abstract: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. We consider terms up to cubic order in curvature, solve the resulting field equations, and find one-way hidden wormholes as numerical solutions: these are regular black holes with an interior wormhole throat that is crossable in one direction and leads to a cosmological spacetime in its interior. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.
papers.summary: The authors construct regular black hole solutions in a four-dimensional effective field theory with cubic curvature terms, revealing a novel one-way hidden wormhole geometry that connects the exterior to a cosmological interior without an inner horizon. These solutions avoid the mass‑inflation instability of conventional regular black holes and offer a new laboratory for studying horizonless wormhole physics in a purely gravitational setting.

papers.title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.authors: Salvatore D. Pace, Sakura Schafer-Nameki, Carolyn Zhang
papers.abstract: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.
papers.summary: SymTFT encodes ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems in a higher-dimensional topological theory, enabling a clean separation of symmetry data from system-specific dynamics. The review surveys how this framework classifies anomalies, gapped phases, and organizes symmetry structures in gapless phases, with extensions to higher dimensions, continuous, fermionic, mixed, and spacetime symmetries.

papers.title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
papers.abstract: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $\rho$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $\rho$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $\rho -1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.
papers.summary: This review extends Luttinger's theorem to fractionalized Fermi liquids, deriving the modified Fermi volume in terms of electron density shifted by a quantized amount linked to spinon fractionalization. It also generalizes Oshikawa's flux insertion argument to systems with emergent gauge fields and discusses implications for gapless spin liquids.

papers.title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding
papers.abstract: The python's lunch conjecture relates the complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks to an exponential cost associated with post-selection. We establish a tight query lower bound for this decoding problem in a Haar random oracle model, with a python's lunch circuit that applies Haar random unitary $U$ to a logical input and fixed ancillas, followed by post-selection on $m$ output qubits. Given one copy of the normalized encoded state and coherent oracle access to $U$ and $U^\dagger$, including controlled queries, we prove that recovering even a single logical bit with constant average advantage requires $\Omega(2^{m/2})$ queries. Together with the state-independent amplitude amplification upper bound for approximately isometric encodings, this establishes query complexity $\Theta(2^{m/2})$ at constant decoding accuracy. We also comment on the decoding cost for other "admissible'" ensembles of unitaries $U$ which give rise to families of approximately isometric holographic maps.
papers.summary: The paper proves a tight query lower bound for decoding in the python's lunch conjecture, showing that recovering a single logical bit requires ≥2^{m/2} queries in a Haar random oracle model. This result establishes the query complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks and connects it to post-selection costs.

papers.title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
papers.abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a new class of rotating boson stars with cyclic symmetry that can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle, achieved through self‑gravitating quantum vortex molecules. These structures offer a relativistic analogue of vortex assemblies in condensates and suggest laboratory realizations of such exotic compact objects.

papers.title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
papers.abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.
papers.summary: The authors construct quantum reference frames in QFT by using localized scalar field modes as frames for the field’s shift symmetry, and compute entropies and correlations of relational observables, revealing that such QRFs are generically mixed and correlated with subsystems. They also propose experimental tests using ultracold atom simulators, linking QRF physics to analogue gravity platforms.

papers.title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
papers.authors: Mrinal Dasgupta, Alexander Fraley, Pier Francesco Monni, Saad Nabeebaccus
papers.abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.
papers.summary: The authors develop a new resummation framework for coherence‑violating logarithms in the transverse‑energy flow of rapidity gaps in Drell‑Yan production, extending the formalism to moderate gap sizes relevant for LHC phenomenology. They find sizable corrections beyond the small‑gap approximation, indicating that existing predictions for color‑singlet processes may need revision.

papers.title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.
papers.summary: The paper shows that quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space cannot be sharply localized, leading to a replacement of strict locality by almost locality and microcausality by rapidly decaying commutators. These results imply that standard QFT axioms must be modified when formulated relative to a quantum reference frame, with potential consequences for operational notions of causality.

papers.title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
papers.abstract: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. Their participation crosses over from localization near the facing boundaries to a collective distribution within each region. Expansion in the adjacent-state canonical basis connects this evolution to progressively weaker, more extended reference modes, including adjacent-halo directions.   Building on the established concentration of long-distance logarithmic negativity into a single canonical pair, we show that its spatial participation is smooth and infrared-dominated despite its ultraviolet canonical structure, a distinction also present in pure-state entanglement modes. These results refine the ultraviolet mode picture by resolving the long-wavelength organization of the oscillators participating in the surviving entanglement. Across the massless dispersions studied, the normalized participation approaches a universal long-distance profile when separation is scaled by the negativity radius. Its detailed form and the entanglement range nevertheless remain sensitive to ultraviolet deformations. Together, these findings distinguish infrared-enhanced correlations from distillable entanglement and reveal the collective spatial organization underlying its persistence at large separation.
papers.summary: This paper studies how infrared fluctuations affect vacuum entanglement in relativistic and Lifshitz harmonic chains, showing that logarithmic negativity remains bounded while mutual information diverges as the mass goes to zero. It identifies collective canonical modes that carry the negativity and maps their spatial distribution, revealing a universal long-distance profile when scaled by the negativity radius.

papers.title: Anomaly inflow for simplicial K\"{a}hler fermions
papers.abstract: We study massive K\"{a}hler Dirac fermions propagating on finite triangulations of various three dimensional manifolds with one or more boundaries. To probe the anomaly structure of these models we decompose the K\"{a}hler field into two reduced K\"{a}hler fields and choose boundary conditions that ensure that any edge modes are necessarily massless. We then show how to factorize the Pfaffian of this system into a product of bulk and boundary sectors each of which can separately pick up a phase under a global $Z_4$ transformation of the fermions that simultaneously changes the sign of the mass. These phases are topological, depending only on the index of the lattice K\"{a}hler operator in that sector. For the boundary sector a non-trivial phase signals the presence of a 't Hooft anomaly. We study cases where the boundary is anomalous but an inflow from the bulk cancels its phase. Canceling this anomaly for a non-orientable boundary in the absence of the bulk recovers the known classification of topological superconductors. We also give a continuum interpretation of these results in terms of inflow from a gravitational Chern Simons theory which is induced by integrating out massive bulk K\"{a}hler Dirac fermions. In the presence of a boundary the latter gives rise to Wen-Zee terms that mediate the anomaly inflow mechanism.
papers.summary: The paper investigates massive Kähler Dirac fermions on triangulated 3‑manifolds, decomposing the field to isolate massless edge modes and analyzing the resulting Pfaffian factorization into bulk and boundary sectors. It demonstrates how a global Z4 transformation induces topological phases tied to the lattice index, with bulk inflow canceling boundary ’t Hooft anomalies and connecting to gravitational Chern–Simons/Wen‑Zee terms.

papers.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
papers.abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces.   Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored.   Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others.   The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.
papers.summary: This work establishes a link between modular quantization and a thermal‑doubled non‑commutative Born geometry using Tomita‑Takesaki theory on complexified ortho‑symplectic spaces, suggesting a new framework for quantum spacetime. It proposes that modular algebraic structures could underlie quantum gravity and hints at CPT‑mirror cosmologies, but does not directly address holography, celestial amplitudes, or number‑theoretic structures.

papers.title: Small-ball asymptotics of Gaussian matrix products: Open Fermi shells and the Grassmannian
papers.abstract: Let $P=A_N\cdots A_1$ be a product of independent standard real or complex Gaussian matrices of arbitrary fixed sizes. For complex entries we determine the exact leading terms, of the form $\kappa\,\varepsilon^C(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$, of the operator-norm and Frobenius small-ball probabilities of $P$, together with the corresponding asymptotics of the Laplace transform of $\|P^2\|_{F}$. The exponent $C$ is the known diversity order, while the logarithmic power follows a filling rule: when fermions are placed on ladders of states determined by the sizes and the last occupied level has degeneracy $\mu$ and contains $h$ particles, $q=h(\mu-h)$. The determinant of this last shell expands in Pl\"ucker coordinates graded by the Schubert cells of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(h,\mu)$, with leading coefficients proportional to normalized degrees of Schubert varieties. For real entries we prove that the Frobenius small-ball probability has an exact positive leading term of order $\varepsilon^{C/2}(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$ and that the operator-norm probability has the same order, which gives a proof of the known real log canonical threshold and its multiplicity that needs no explicit resolution of singularities. We evaluate the real leading coefficient in closed form for every shell with at most one logarithm, a class that contains all products of two factors, and we conjecture its general form, which agrees with the classical constant of vector chains. Applications include the outage probability of cascaded multi-antenna channels at high signal-to-noise ratio and the Bayesian evidence of deep linear networks.
papers.summary: The paper derives precise small‑ball asymptotics for products of independent Gaussian matrices, revealing that the leading terms involve powers of the error probability and logarithmic corrections governed by a filling rule on the Grassmannian. It connects these results to operator‑norm and Frobenius norms, Schubert calculus, and practical applications such as outage probabilities in multi‑antenna channels and Bayesian evidence for deep linear networks.

papers.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.
